name: Short-Stay Visa (Category C) & Visa-Exempt Arrangements

requirements.blocker_text: This requires showing you'll leave Ireland at the end of your visit. IMPORTANT: Ireland is NOT part of Schengen — a Schengen visa is NOT valid for travel to Ireland, and Ireland maintains its own separate visa-required list.

This allows nationals of China or India to travel around the Common Travel Area on a single UK or Irish short-stay visa endorsed 'BIVS' — no separate Irish visa needed if already holding a qualifying UK visa, or vice versa.

evidence_required.document: Evidence of sufficient funds and intent to leave

outcome.duration_length: up to 90 days; not renewable/extendable except in emergencies
outcome.physical_presence_requirement: not valid for travel to any Schengen-area country; a separate Schengen visa would be needed for onward Schengen travel

sources.title: Visa requirements for entering Ireland - Department of Foreign Affairs

notes: GENUINE STRUCTURAL CONFIRMATION, the last and one of the most foundational facts closing out this entire 15-country dataset: Ireland is an EU member state but explicitly NOT part of Schengen (it opted out and maintains the Common Travel Area with the UK instead — see ie_common_travel_area) — a Schengen visa issued by any other EU state is NOT valid for travel to Ireland, and Ireland runs its own independent visa-required nationality list rather than inheriting the Schengen one. This is the exact structural inverse of Switzerland (a non-EU country that IS in Schengen, ch_tourist_visa), making these two countries' visit-visa routes a genuinely instructive contrasting pair for anyone comparing the 'visit' category across this full multi-country dataset. British-Irish Visa Scheme (BIVS) confirmed still operational for China and India specifically — a real, narrow, named-country exception allowing single-visa travel around the CTA, legal basis the Immigration Act (Visas) Order 2014 as amended by SI 502/2016. Fees not fully confirmed at tier-1 precision during the underlying research (tier-3 sources cited roughly €60 single-entry / €100 multiple-entry) — flagged as a gap rather than asserted with false confidence, the same honest-gap convention used throughout this entire dataset build.
